key_insight: PING combines graph neural networks with advection–diffusion physics to forecast transport on irregular sensor networks and support solar power forecasting.
engineering_relevance: Better cloud-motion forecasts can improve intra-day photovoltaic power predictions and help integrate more solar generation into the grid.
method: Represent transported particle concentrations as signals on an irregular graph.
Use a discretized advection–diffusion equation as a soft constraint in the training loss.
Couple PING with PV forecasting models using ground-sensor and satellite cloud data.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance on par with state-of-the-art models on synthetic and real transport datasets, including sea surface temperature and cloud index data, plus improved intra-day PV forecasting.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical PV forecasting gains, so deployment benefits require site-specific validation.
paper_title: PING: physics informed graph neural network for advection-diffusion processes with applications to solar power forecasting
